intro: Things made in Egypt that you can watch being made, buy or try on your trip: where each is made, where you find it and who makes it. Every item names its source and the day we last checked it.
disclosure: EgyBI takes no payment, commission or gift from any maker or shop on this page, and none of these links earns us anything.
method: We list a craft or a maker only when a named source describes it: the maker's own site, an official or academic page, or the press. A price or a tip on telling the real thing from an imitation appears only when a source gives it, with that source beside it. Where we found no website or account for a maker, we say so rather than guess one. We link to the makers instead of copying their pictures. Warnings about shops come from several travellers' reports, and say so.

rows.what: Panels of cut cloth stitched by hand onto a backing, made to line tents and now hung as wall pieces.
rows.made: The covered Street of the Tentmakers, just south of Bab Zuwayla, Cairo.
rows.find: The tentmakers' shops on that street, where the stitching is done in the shopfronts.
rows.watch: Yes: the makers work in their shops.
rows.source: TRC Leiden: Street of the Tentmakers, Cairo

rows.item: Brass, copper and silver work, and lanterns
rows.what: Engraved plates, hand-made brass lanterns and silver jewellery, made in small workshops of the old city.
rows.made: Al-Muizz Street and the lanes behind Al-Azhar Mosque, Cairo.
rows.find: Workshops upstairs and behind the shopfronts of Khan el-Khalili and Al-Muizz Street.
rows.watch: In some workshops, if you ask.

genuine.text: Many shops sell factory-made pieces that look handmade, so ask the maker how a piece was made.

rows.source: National Geographic: a guide to Cairo's craft heritage (24 Aug 2023)

rows.what: Wooden boxes and tables set with pieces of shell in geometric patterns.
rows.made: Workshops in the Al-Azhar quarter, Cairo.
rows.find: Shops of Khan el-Khalili and Al-Muizz Street.

genuine.text: Cheap boxes often use plastic in place of shell or bone.

rows.source: National Geographic: a guide to Cairo's craft heritage (24 Aug 2023)

rows.what: Cups, vases and lamps blown by hand from recycled glass, in family workshops.
rows.made: Workshops near the Qaitbay complex in the City of the Dead, Cairo.
rows.find: Shops in Khan el-Khalili, which many of the workshops sell through.
rows.source: Africanews: Egyptian craftsmen preserve century-old glassblowing (7 Sep 2023)

rows.what: Pots and tableware thrown on the wheel by Cairo's potters, who were moved into a purpose-built village.
rows.made: The Fustat pottery village behind the Mosque of Amr ibn al-As, Old Cairo: 152 workshops, opened in November 2021.
rows.find: The workshops of the pottery village.
rows.source: Cairo Governorate: opening of the Fustat pottery village (2021)

rows.what: Rugs, quilts and bags woven and stitched by women from cloth-factory offcuts, through a non-profit working since the 1980s.
rows.made: Manshiyat Naser, Cairo, by the Association for the Protection of the Environment (APE).
rows.find: Souq El Fustat in Old Cairo and the Fair Trade Egypt shops.
rows.maker: Fair Trade Egypt, which sells APE's work
rows.source: SceneNow: how APE is empowering the women of Mokattam (9 Jul 2022)

rows.what: Wool and cotton tapestries woven freehand by village weavers, without a drawing to follow, at an art centre founded for the purpose.
rows.made: The Ramses Wissa Wassef Art Centre, Harraniya village, on the Saqqara road, Giza.
rows.find: At the centre itself, which sells directly. It says it is open daily from 10:00 to 16:00, Mondays by appointment.
rows.watch: Yes: the centre invites visitors to meet the weavers.
rows.source: Ramses Wissa Wassef Art Centre (its own site)

rows.what: Painted pottery from a village school started by the Swiss potter Evelyne Porret, now run by the village's own potters.
rows.made: Tunis village, on the edge of Lake Qarun, Fayoum.
rows.find: The village's studios. The village holds a pottery festival each year, usually in November.
rows.watch: Yes: almost any workshop offers a one-day class, and your fired pieces are ready about a week later.
rows.source: Egyptian Streets: things to do in Tunis village, Fayoum (17 Dec 2020)

rows.what: Vases and bowls carved by hand from Egyptian alabaster (calcite), a trade passed down in West Bank families.
rows.made: Workshops in El Qurna, on Luxor's West Bank.
rows.find: The workshops along the road between the Valley of the Kings and Deir el-Bahari, and the Luxor souk.
rows.watch: Yes: workshops carve at their entrances.

genuine.text: Real alabaster lets light through: a thin piece glows when you hold it up to the light.

rows.maker: Hapi for Alabaster, El Qurna (no website or account found)
rows.source: Outlook Traveller: inside El Qurna's alabaster legacy (updated 29 Dec 2025)

rows.what: Cloth woven on hand looms in the towns of Upper Egypt, listed by UNESCO in 2020 as heritage in urgent need of safeguarding.
rows.made: Akhmim (Sohag) and Naqada (Qena), among other towns.
rows.find: We found no published way to visit the weavers; their work is sold at craft fairs and shops in Cairo.
rows.maker: Association of Upper Egypt for Education and Development, which runs the Akhmim centre (no website found)
rows.source: UNESCO: Egypt's elements on the intangible heritage lists

rows.what: Palm-frond baskets and fans, beadwork and weaving sold in the Nubian villages of Aswan's West Bank.
rows.made: Aswan, in Nubian villages such as Gharb Soheil.
rows.find: The market at Gharb Soheil, which is built for visitors.
rows.source: Egyptian Streets: the ultimate guide to souvenir shopping in Egypt (4 Dec 2024)

rows.what: Garments and cloth hand-embroidered by Siwan women, through a programme started in 1999 by Laila Neamatalla.
rows.made: Siwa Oasis.
rows.find: The Siwa Creations showroom in Zamalek, Cairo, and the Grand Egyptian Museum gift shop.
rows.source: Egyptian Streets: Siwan women stitch their heritage into global fashion (6 Nov 2025)

rows.what: Lamps and objects carved from the rock salt of Siwa's salt lakes, a small local industry.
rows.made: Siwa Oasis.
rows.find: Bazaars in Siwa town.
rows.source: Egypt Today: Siwan salt lamps (2017)

rows.what: Dates of Siwa's own varieties, such as Siwi, Frehi and Azzawi, grown by the oasis's farmers and protected by a Slow Food Presidium.
rows.made: Siwa Oasis, through a producers' association of 87 farmers.
rows.find: Siwa town. We found no Siwa date brand with its own website.
rows.source: Slow Food Foundation: Siwa Oasis dates

rows.what: Bags, clothes and cloth embroidered by Jebeliya Bedouin women, through a group named FanSina.
rows.made: St Catherine, South Sinai.
rows.find: St Catherine town. FanSina's old website no longer works, and we found no other account.
rows.source: Daily News Egypt: FanSina, the art of Sinai

rows.what: Long-staple cotton grown in Egypt. The Egyptian Cotton mark says a product is 100% Egyptian cotton; it does not say where the product was made.
rows.made: The cotton is grown in Egypt; licensed products are made in many countries.
rows.find: Shops across Egypt; check the label rather than the shop's word.

genuine.text: A genuine product carries the mark and a licence number, which you can check on the association's verify page.
genuine.source: Egyptian Cotton Association: verify a licence

rows.source: Egyptian Cotton Association: the Egyptian Cotton mark

rows.what: Jewellery drawing on Egyptian and Islamic design, which the house says is handcrafted by local craftsmen at its workshop in Cairo.
rows.made: The house's workshop in Cairo.
rows.find: Its boutiques, including one inside the Grand Egyptian Museum.
rows.source: Azza Fahmy: craftsmanship (its own site)

rows.what: Flat-woven kilim rugs and cushions made by local weavers, from a studio founded in 2016.
rows.made: Fowa, Kafr El Sheikh, in the Nile Delta.
rows.find: Sold through its own website; we found no published showroom.
rows.source: Kiliim (its own site)

rows.what: Bags and furniture covered in Plastex, a cloth hand-woven on manual looms from discarded plastic bags.
rows.made: Cairo, with home-based craftswomen.
rows.find: The shops listed on its own website.
rows.source: Dubai Design Week: regional design studio wins Ro Plastic Prize

rows.what: Bags made from recycled plastic bags and bottles, worked with the waste collectors of Manshiyat Naser.
rows.made: Cairo.
rows.find: The shops listed on its own website.
rows.source: Up-Fuse (its own site)

rows.what: Handmade home goods from a workshop that trains local and refugee artisans in Egypt.
rows.made: 6th of October City, Giza.
rows.find: Its own shop, which says it opens Sunday to Thursday, 9:00 to 17:00.
rows.source: Yadawee (its own site)

groups.title: Food to take home
groups.note: Britain lets travellers bring dates without a plant health certificate, but no meat or dairy; honey up to 2 kg. Check your own country's rules before you pack food.
groups.note_source: GOV.UK: bringing food into Great Britain

rows.what: Extra-virgin olive oil from an Egyptian producer whose groves lie south of Alexandria; it won a gold award at the New York olive oil competition in 2018.
rows.made: Groves south of Alexandria.
rows.find: Supermarkets in Egypt.
rows.source: Olive Oil Times: Egyptian EVOO pioneer sets gold standard

rows.what: Dried hibiscus flowers for the red tea drunk across Egypt, hot or cold. One organic brand, ISIS, grows its own in the Bahariya Oasis.
rows.made: The Bahariya Oasis, for the ISIS brand.
rows.find: Supermarkets, and the spice stalls of Khan el-Khalili.
rows.source: SEKEM: ISIS Organic company profile (2017)

rows.what: Spices, herbs and dried flowers sold by weight. Egypt's spice markets sell what is grown here and what is imported, so ask where a spice comes from.
rows.made: Various.
rows.find: The Attareen spice market and the spice alleys next to Khan el-Khalili, Cairo.
rows.source: Egyptian Streets: Egypt's famous herbs and spices (21 Feb 2022)

rows.what: Egyptian sweets and festival biscuits (kahk) from a Cairo patisserie that opened its first shop in 1974.
rows.made: Cairo.
rows.find: Its shops in Cairo and Giza, the first on Talaat Harb Street, downtown.
rows.source: El Abd: about us (its own site)

rows.what: A shop that sells the work of named Egyptian producer groups, such as the Armant Women Group and APE, at fixed prices.
rows.find: 27 Yehia Ibrahim Street, Zamalek, Cairo, and a second shop in Nasr City.
rows.source: Fair Trade Egypt (its own site)

rows.what: A family-owned shop, open since 1985, that buys directly from artisan families across Egypt: Sinai Bedouin work, Fayoum pottery, Siwa embroidery.
rows.find: 14 Mohamed Abdel Wahab Street, Zamalek, Cairo.
rows.source: Nomad Gallery: about us (its own site)

rows.what: A covered market of craft shops in Old Cairo, with fixed prices: glass, leather, copper, wood, textiles and jewellery.
rows.find: Next to the Mosque of Amr ibn al-As, Old Cairo.
rows.source: CairoScene: the textile shops of Souq El Fustat (8 Mar 2026)

rows.item: The Grand Egyptian Museum gift shop
rows.what: The museum's shop stocks crafts from Fayoum, Upper Egypt and the Delta beside its replicas.
rows.find: The Grand Egyptian Museum, Giza.
rows.source: CairoScene: inside the Grand Egyptian Museum's gift shop (13 Nov 2025)

rows.what: Egypt's yearly handicrafts fair, run by the state's small-business agency, with more than a thousand exhibitors. Entry was free in 2025.
rows.find: The Egypt International Exhibition Center, New Cairo, each October.
rows.source: Egyptian Streets: Turathna exhibition 2025 (2 Oct 2025)

groups.title: Shops travellers warn about
groups.note: These are reports by several travellers, not EgyBI's own findings. Many guided tours stop at shops; you can ask your guide to skip them.

rows.what: Many reviewers describe a short demonstration followed by a long sales pitch, and prices that drop by more than half once you haggle. Real papyrus is made from papyrus stalks; cheap copies are printed on banana leaf.
rows.source: Tripadvisor: Papyrus Institute, Giza, travellers' reviews

rows.what: Reviewers of one Cairo perfume factory, now closed, describe diluted oils and bottles swapped after paying. The same kind of stop is still sold inside shopping tours.
rows.source: Tripadvisor: Perfume Factory, Cairo, travellers' reviews

rows.what: Several reviewers report high mark-ups, pressure to buy and guides taking a commission; others report no pressure. Agree the total before paying.
rows.source: Tripadvisor: Imhotep Alabaster, Luxor, travellers' reviews

rows.what: Reviewers say many of the trinkets at the market's entrance stalls are imported; Egyptian handwork is found deeper in, in the workshops and on the Street of the Tentmakers.
rows.source: Tripadvisor: Khan el-Khalili, travellers' reviews
